reference.title: Scenario 11 — Image with Floating Label <div> Elements Layered on Top
reference.shortdesc: Scenario 11 — Image with Floating Label <div> Elements Layered on Top Consider a document

section.p:
Consider a document where an element is inserted into the document body and multiple
elements are positioned on top of the image using CSS (for example, position: absolute) to create labels, admonitions, or annotations.

entry.codeblock:
Database Server
Application Server
Load Balancer

<fig> <image href="media/network_topology.png"> <alt>Network topology</alt> </image> </fig> <!-- Positioned/overlaid text labels ("Database Server", "Application Server", "Load Balancer") have no DITA equivalent for absolutely-positioned text and cannot be converted automatically; flagged for manual review. -->

section.p:
Result: The converter extracts and preserves the element itself because it exists as a valid image reference. However, the CSS-positioned
labels layered above the image are ignored during conversion.
section.note: For annotated diagrams, embed labels directly into the image before inserting it into the HTML page.
